text:
Brayden Schenn is 35, a Stanley Cup winner in St. Louis, now a mentor on Long Island. The New York Post wrote about him "paying it forward" with prospect Victor Eklund. On the ice he has 15 points in 22 games, including a three-point night against the Kings that ended a four-game winless streak for the Islanders.

The points are ahead of the play. He's shooting 18.2%, above his likely range of 12% to 17%, and the Islanders have scored 6.5 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. At 5v5 they get under 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, more than 7 points worse than when he sits.

His own shots are fine: 6 goals on 5.8 expected, from the dangerous areas he's always worked. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him leaving his zone with the puck on 68% of exits last season, a clean breakout game. But Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level, and this year's luck is doing a lot of lifting. Watch whether the points hold as the bounces even out.
headline: Schenn's veteran bounce, with an asterisk
